title_en: MacroVoices #557 Michael Every: The Blue Tsunami Lands on Markets... and Geopolitics
title_zh: Michael Every（Rabobank）：蓝色海啸登陆市场与地缘政治
subtitle_zh: 民主党中期选举大胜后，Michael Every 解读其对伊朗、乌克兰局势、能源与市场的连锁冲击。
summary_zh: 本期 MacroVoices 由 Eric Townsend 与 Patrick Ceresna 对话 Rabobank 地缘战略学家 Michael Every，聚焦美国中期选举的「蓝色海啸」（blue tsunami）——民主党拿下国会两院——及其对市场的连锁冲击。Every 强调，发生在美国的事不会只停留在美国：一个被不愿再看冒险行为的国会所束缚的美国，将成为受到极大约束的地缘政治角色。他梳理伊朗战争的可能光谱，从终极的 TACO（Trump Always Chickens Out）到美国全面抽身；届时「权力最厌恶真空」，要么伊朗联合俄罗斯、中国、朝鲜填补，要么以色列、土耳其自我主张，两种情形短期内都不构成能源价格走低的理由。对于以色列作为核国家在失去美国常规支持下的核升级风险，Every 认为那只是极其「肥尾」（fat tail）的尾部风险。节目还谈及钱袋子的权力（power of the purse）、国会与总统之间可能历史级别的开战权冲突、关税作为新重商主义（neo-mercantilist）再工业化几乎唯一途径的角色，以及 Trump 版共和党难赢 2028、甚至出现由 Marjorie Taylor Greene、Tucker Carlson 等昔日盟友牵头的第三党的可能。结尾 Trading Desk 指出债市并未有意义地移动、黄金只是超卖反弹回 4000 美元上方。

turns.zh: 你可能不仅迎来新一届国会，还会迎来一位新总统。所以那并不能真正解决任何问题，尽管升级也没有任何保证一定能解决。但我认为，现在显然比以前有更高的概率，Trump 会来这么一出 TACO／‘整份 enchilada’，说‘好，来个象征性的行动，然后我就撤’。

turns.en: But I have to emphasize or re-emphasize, I don't think that is going to bring energy prices down sustainably the way that the US would like to see. And I don't think it's better for the US geostrategic position, much unlike the position that many of the people who voted in the election would like to see.
turns.zh: 但我必须强调、或者说再次强调：我不认为那会让能源价格以美国希望看到的方式可持续地下跌；我也不认为这对美国的地缘战略地位更好——这与很多在这次选举中投票的人所希望看到的立场大相径庭。

turns.en: So there is a common understanding, and if I were American, I would feel very much the same way. Don't get me wrong. But if we just vote, no, we don't have any more wars. We won't have any more wars. Well, unfortunately, being anti-war doesn't prevent war. You know, the old Latin phrase is, see this patch and parabellum.
turns.zh: 所以这里存在一种共识，而如果我是美国人，我也会有非常相同的感受，别误会我。但如果我们只是投票说‘不，我们不要再有任何战争了’，我们就不会再有战争了吗？很不幸，反战并不能阻止战争。你知道那句古老的拉丁语：si vis pacem para bellum。

turns.en: If you want peace, prepare for war. And I say that as someone who's certainly no neocon, before anyone who tries to ascribe a belief system to me, and who is passionately opposed to the second Gulf War, by the way, just over 20 years ago. So that's my track record on that. But the theoretical framework of just saying,
turns.zh: 如果你想要和平，就要为战争做好准备。我这么说，是作为一个绝非‘新保守主义者’（neocon）的人——免得有人试图把某套信仰体系硬安到我头上——而且顺便说一句，我是一个在 20 多年前就激烈反对第二次海湾战争的人。这就是我在那件事上的过往记录。但那种‘我们只是说

turns.en: we don't want war, therefore you won't get it, isn't how the world works when you're hedging one. Well, let's imagine that the US did pull back or not escalate. It seems to me that that really probably means that Ukraine would continue to strike Russian oil refineries because it's the US that's been trying to restrain that.
turns.zh: 我们不想要战争，于是你就不会得到战争’的理论框架，在你只是在对冲时并不是世界运转的方式。好，我们设想一下美国确实收缩、或不升级的情形。在我看来，那很可能真的意味着乌克兰会继续打击俄罗斯的炼油厂，因为一直以来试图克制这件事的正是美国。

turns.en: And although I feel like I've been misunderstood by a lot of our listeners sending angry emails, I'm not rooting for Russia in the conflict. I'm just saying if you strike oil refineries anywhere in the world, you're reducing global refining capacity and crack spreads will stay elevated,
turns.zh: 而且，尽管我觉得自己被很多给我们发愤怒邮件的听众误解了——我并不是在这场冲突中给俄罗斯加油。我只是说，如果你在世界任何地方打击炼油厂，你就在削减全球炼油产能，而裂解价差（crack spreads）将维持在高位，

turns.en: dramatically elevated for years after the war is over. So let's imagine that there is kind of a pullback in terms of participation in this war. What does that mean in terms of the refineries strikes and crack spread will outlook? It can only be bullish for that particular crack spread.
turns.zh: 在战争结束后数年里都戏剧性地高企。那么，我们设想一下，在这场战争的参与上出现某种收缩。这对炼油厂遭袭和裂解价差的前景意味着什么？对那个特定的裂解价差而言，只可能是利多的。

turns.en: And therefore you have to ask yourself how likely is it? And again, we've already touched on this, but in order to get the de-escalation deal, even if it's just a frozen conflict, North Korea, South Korea style, which I think is the best you're going to get. To get that done, you need obviously the US standing behind it.
turns.zh: 因此你就得问自己：这有多大可能？同样，我们已经谈到过，但为了达成降级协议——哪怕只是朝鲜、韩国式的‘冻结冲突’（frozen conflict），我认为那是你能拿到的最好结果——要办成这件事，显然你需要美国在背后撑腰。

turns.en: And you need Russia and Ukraine to both agree, otherwise the war goes on. So Ukraine, seeing Trump is weaker, may or may not think now is the time to make a deal. But Russia almost certainly will look around and say, well, why now? Trump will be even weaker six months from now. So maybe he'll have to come back to us
turns.zh: 而且你需要俄罗斯和乌克兰双方都同意，否则战争就继续。所以乌克兰看到 Trump 变弱了，可能觉得、也可能不觉得现在是达成协议的时机。但俄罗斯几乎肯定会环顾四周说：‘那为什么是现在？六个月后 Trump 会更弱。所以他也许不得不以

turns.en: on far, far weaker terms and we'll be able to strike a harder bargain. So in that particular way, the logic suggests to me that while any outcome is still possible, the probability is more likely that we get more escalation on that particular front. And potentially, as I just said, at the same time as we get escalation in the Middle East,
turns.zh: 弱得多的条件回来找我们，我们就能敲定一份更苛刻的交易。’所以在这个特定意义上，逻辑向我表明：尽管任何结果都仍有可能，但概率上更可能的是，我们在那条特定战线上看到更多升级。而且潜在地，正如我刚说的，与此同时中东也在升级，

turns.en: at which point, yeah, crack spreads stay high and frankly, so do energy prices until there's some kind of resolution. Now, that doesn't mean, of course, the Middle East war rages forever. It could be that the US manages to succeed in what it's doing and which point, they would come down sharply on that front
turns.zh: 到那时，是的，裂解价差维持在高位，坦白说能源价格也是，直到出现某种解决方案。当然，这并不意味着中东战争会永远打下去。也有可能美国成功达成它正在做的事，那样一来，在那条战线上价格会急剧回落；

turns.en: or things are destabilized to the point where other players are getting sucked in. Then you have a long running destabilizing, rolling conflict there, similar to what we have now to an extent, but slightly different partners or slightly different players playing in different ways. And again, that supports energy prices.
turns.zh: 或者局势动荡到其他玩家被卷入的地步。那样你就会有一场长期、持续失稳、滚动式的冲突，在某种程度上类似我们现在的情形，但伙伴略有不同、玩家略有不同、玩法也不同。而这同样支撑能源价格。

turns.en: So I'm not poo-pooing any of the trading-based fundamentals that we've seen recently. They make a lot of sense. And we are seeing really historic headlines which deserve historic price swings. But I don't see the dove of peace, you know, flying through the air with Nolly Branch in its peak at the moment, unfortunately.
turns.zh: 所以我并不是在贬低我们最近看到的任何基于交易的基本面。它们很有道理。而且我们确实正看到配得上历史性价格波动的历史性头条。但很遗憾，我此刻并没有看到那只衔着橄榄枝、在空中翱翔的和平鸽。

turns.en: A lot of your framing of everything has been around economic state craft changing everything and the old playbook being dead. It seems like the new playbook is probably dying as well. So is there a new new playbook? Well, there's going to have to be. And the first thing I want to say on that front is that when I dub grand macro strategy,
turns.zh: 你对一切的很多框架，都是围绕‘经济治国术’（economic statecraft）正在改变一切、旧剧本已死。看起来新剧本大概也在消亡。那么，有没有一个‘新新剧本’？嗯，势必得有一个。在这点上我想说的第一件事是，当我提出‘宏大宏观策略’（grand macro strategy）时——

turns.en: which is grand strategy, the old international relations concept and macro strategy, which is obviously market-facing stuff. So that's where the, you know, the portmanteau of grand macro strategy comes from. That was something that I certainly believed and continued to believe was something that the U at the White House was utilizing.
turns.zh: 它是‘大战略’（grand strategy，那个旧的国际关系概念）加上‘宏观策略’（macro strategy，显然是面向市场的东西），‘宏大宏观策略’这个合成词就是这么来的。那确实是我一直相信、并持续相信白宫正在运用的一套东西。

turns.en: But that doesn't mean for a moment that every grand macro strategy is guaranteed success and every aspect of what it's doing. And that doesn't mean there can't be inherent contradictions. Just as there are in any political platform, whether it's international or domestic. And you can certainly see that the lack of the focus
turns.zh: 但这绝不意味着每一套宏大宏观策略在它所做的每一个方面都保证成功；也不意味着它内部不可能存在固有的矛盾——就像任何政治纲领内部都存在矛盾一样，无论是国际的还是国内的。你当然能看到，那种缺乏对

turns.en: on affordability, the lack of the ability to get this war done and dusted very quickly, like Venezuela, because as an aside, the message is, yes, the US doesn't like war. The US didn't have quite such a problem with Venezuela, the special military operation, because that was over in two or three days with absolutely minimal bloodshed.
turns.zh: 可负担性（affordability）的关注、缺乏非常快地把这场战争干净利落收尾的能力——就像 Venezuela 那样，因为顺便说一句，传递出的信息是：是的，美国不喜欢战争；但美国对 Venezuela 那次‘特别军事行动’并没有那么大的意见，因为它两三天就结束了，几乎没流什么血。

turns.en: So it's not the interjection to other countries, perhaps, as the problem is, doing it and not winning or not winning quickly. But if you're not going to win quickly, then you need to pivot. And clearly, over the past couple of months, there hasn't been a good plan B for what to do next
turns.zh: 所以问题也许并不在于干涉其他国家，而在于‘打了却赢不了、或赢不够快’。但如果你没法速胜，那你就需要转向（pivot）。而显然，在过去几个月里，并没有一个好的 B 计划来应对接下来该做什么，

turns.en: to make sure you don't get a shell-acking in the midterms. And from these midterms onwards, that grand macro strategy will have to change again. Energy is going to have to be looked at. But again, you won't get lower energy prices just by saying, guess what? I don't want war and I'm sorry. If that were the case, it would be wonderful.
turns.zh: 以确保你不会在中期选举里挨一顿痛击。而从这届中期选举往后，那套宏大宏观策略将不得不再次改变，能源将不得不被重新审视。但同样，你不会仅仅通过说‘你猜怎么着？我不想要战争了，对不起’就得到更低的能源价格。如果那样就行，那当然太好了。

turns.en: And we really could de-escalate everything very quickly. But to do it, you have to give up so much geostrategic advantage in other areas that there is a very serious cost across the entire economic and military industrial complex going forward. It's pretty hard to recover from. That's why I argued all year up until recently
turns.zh: 而且我们真的能非常快地给一切降级。但要这么做，你就得在其他领域放弃如此之多的地缘战略优势，以至于整个经济和军工复合体往后都要付出非常严重的代价，而且很难从中恢复。这就是为什么我一整年、直到最近都在主张

turns.en: that Trump wouldn't do a taco. That still holds. So we have to consider that very strongly. Let's touch not just on energy, but also on food and fertilizer flows through hormones. This is something we've talked about before. And I've been quite surprised. It's at least so far the food price, the looking at grain prices and so forth.
turns.zh: Trump 不会来一出 TACO。这一点仍然成立。所以我们必须非常认真地把这一点纳入考量。让我们不只谈能源，也谈谈经由霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）的粮食和化肥流动。这是我们以前聊过的话题。我一直挺惊讶的——至少到目前为止，粮食价格、看谷物价格等等，

turns.en: We haven't seen that transmission of fertilizer affecting grain prices or even the term structure of grain prices. That expectation I was thinking would get built into the market of much higher grain prices. Doesn't seem to be materializing. What do you think is going on there? Well, it's a complex picture.
turns.zh: 我们并没有看到化肥向谷物价格、甚至谷物价格期限结构（term structure）的传导。我原以为那种‘谷物价格会大幅走高’的预期会被计入市场，但它似乎并没有成真。你觉得那里到底在发生什么？嗯，这是一幅复杂的图景。

turns.en: Robert Bank is fortunate to have some of the world's leading experts on that particular field working for them. And I'm not one. So therefore, I don't want to take too much of their work in vain. All I will say is that it's been complex and to do with the timing of agricultural seasons and expectations
turns.zh: Rabobank 有幸拥有一些该领域全球顶尖的专家为其效力，而我不是其中之一。所以我不想过多地妄评他们的工作。我只会说，这件事一直很复杂，与农业季节的时点、以及对这场冲突会持续多久的预期有关，

turns.en: about how long this will or won't last. Stock depletion and demand destruction. In some cases, so it's an interaction of all of them. But if we do continue to see sulfur prices where they are and were we to get further sustained destruction of the energy complex globally, obviously, with a lag, things could still change on that front.
turns.zh: 还涉及库存消耗，以及在某些情况下的需求破坏（demand destruction）。所以这是所有这些因素相互作用的结果。但如果我们确实继续看到硫磺价格停在当前水平，而且全球能源体系进一步遭受持续破坏，那么显然，经过一段滞后，那方面仍可能发生变化。

turns.en: What I would like to do, actually, if I may, is pivot to something that I think is a good middle ground between what you've just asked there and what I was just alluding to in terms of grand macro strategy and possible shifts in it. And one of them is something else that's come up in the post-election appraisals, which is tariffs.
turns.zh: 其实，如果可以的话，我想转到一个我认为介于你刚才所问、与我刚才提到的宏大宏观策略及其可能转变之间的一个不错的中间地带。其中之一，是另一件在选后评估中冒出来的东西，那就是关税。

turns.en: Now, they were controversial in 2025, if you remember. And at the time, I said, wait for 2026, things are going to be a lot wilder and they are. I think this could, and I stress could, be a potential window for a change in the tariff regime, but not a removal of the concept of the tariff regime.
turns.zh: 如果你还记得，它们在 2025 年就很有争议。当时我就说‘等着看 2026 吧，事情会狂野得多’，而它们确实如此。我认为这可能——我强调是‘可能’——是关税体制（tariff regime）发生改变的一个潜在窗口，但不是把‘关税体制’这个概念整个取消。

turns.en: Because if we do what I just did on the geopolitical front, which is to say, what happens if I put up my hand and say, let's reverse this. No more of this. I want the easy out. Do I get the answer that I want? And the answer is, no, you don't. You don't get the solution for the resolution that you want.
turns.zh: 因为，如果我们在关税上做我刚才在地缘政治上做的那种事，也就是举手说‘我们把这个逆转吧，别再搞了，我想要简单的出路’，我会得到我想要的答案吗？答案是：不，你不会。你不会得到你想要的那个解决方案或结果。

turns.en: Does it work on the geoeconomic front? If America were to say, you know, Trump's tariffs are a disaster. Let's say Congress passes anti-tariff legislation on new tariff legislation that changes the powers that Trump currently has. Some Republicans help, and he has to decide whether to veto it
turns.zh: 在地缘经济战线上行得通吗？如果美国说‘你知道，Trump 的关税是一场灾难’，假设国会通过反关税立法、或改变 Trump 目前所拥有的权力的新关税立法，一些共和党人帮了忙，于是他必须决定是否否决它，

turns.en: or not, and they manage to even overturn the veto. Let's just imagine that, which is not totally impossible, but it's unlikely. What does that do? Well, OK, let's say you remove the tariff regime. First of all, obviously, you remove some income from a government that's already struggling to raise it.
turns.zh: 而他们甚至设法推翻了他的否决。我们就设想一下——这并非完全不可能，但可能性不大。那会带来什么？好吧，假设你取消了关税体制。首先，显然你从一个本就挣扎着筹资的政府那里拿走了一部分收入。

turns.en: And you reduce the cost of things, short term. Absolutely, you do. Undeniably, removing tariffs will lower costs. You also remove any leverage you have to try and re-industrialize. Because frankly, unless you're going to throw subsidies at industries, which is just as expensive and in a different way, tariffs are, historically,
turns.zh: 而且短期内你会降低东西的成本，这一点绝对没错、无可否认——取消关税会降低成本。但你同时也放弃了任何用来试图重新工业化的筹码。因为坦白说，除非你要往各个行业砸补贴（而那同样昂贵，只是方式不同），否则从历史上看，关税，

turns.en: as Neo-McCantilist history shows, pretty much the only way, alongside other aspects of industrial policy, that you are going to re-industrialize. And if the US isn't going to do that, with or without AI helping to keep labor costs down, how is it going to maintain a resilient economy and an economy capable of supporting
turns.zh: 正如新重商主义历史所表明的，几乎是——连同产业政策的其他方面——你实现重新工业化的唯一途径。而如果美国不这么做，无论有没有 AI 帮着压低劳动力成本，它又要怎么维持一个有韧性的经济、一个有能力支撑

turns.en: the vast military industrial complex that it needs to be global policeman, global hegemon? And the answer is, over time, it isn't. We already see that now. That wouldn't happen in five minutes. But if you project the dots forward, you are accelerating the decline of America's global hegemon,
turns.zh: 它作为全球警察、全球霸主（global hegemon）所需的庞大军工复合体的经济呢？答案是：随着时间推移，它维持不了。我们现在已经看到了。这不会在五分钟之内发生，但如果你把这些点向前延伸，你就是在加速美国全球霸权的衰落。

turns.en: which I can tell you, again, is not a painless exit through the gift shop, where you get to basically be an isolationist peacenick, just making the peace sign at everybody and enjoying a nice way of life with far more affordability. Quite the opposite. Again, the zero-subnature of access to some resources
turns.zh: 而我还可以告诉你，那也不是一次‘从礼品店无痛离场’——你并不能就此当一个孤立主义的‘和平主义者’（peacenick），对着所有人比出和平手势、享受着一种可负担性高得多的美好生活。恰恰相反。同样，对某些资源获取的‘零和’性质

turns.en: would mean that America could likely be much, much worse off, even if there are high economic costs to support the military industrial complex, the way that it has been done over the past 40 years. The two are not directly opposite to each other. There are other ways of doing things. So I don't necessarily see it.
turns.zh: 意味着美国很可能会变得糟糕得多、糟糕得多，即便维持军工复合体、维持过去 40 年那种运作方式有着高昂的经济成本。这两者并不是直接对立的，还有别的做事方式。所以我不一定认为

turns.en: That's going to work either. Therefore, what I think could be logical, and I'm hypothesizing, is you could see some kind of bargain being struck, where Trump says, look, I like my removing some tariffs, but I want to keep the ones on China. And I want to keep the ones for transshipment on China.
turns.zh: 那也行得通。因此，我认为可能是合乎逻辑的——这只是我的假设——你可能会看到某种‘讨价还价’达成：Trump 说‘看，我愿意取消一些关税，但我想保留对中国的那些，也想保留针对中国转口贸易（transshipment）的那些。’

turns.en: And I want to therefore offer the same deal to other parties, for example, Europe, which is very close to introducing aggressive new tariff legislation against China. Why don't we have the same external tariff, and we'll tariff each other less? So in other words, what I thought Trump was trying to do
turns.zh: ‘因此我想把同样的交易提供给其他各方，比如 Europe——它非常接近出台针对中国的激进新关税立法。我们为什么不用同样的对外关税，然后彼此之间少征点关税呢？’换句话说，也就是我原以为 Trump 试图

turns.en: with the USMCA, where Canada is the holdout, and with the Americas, where now Brazil, obviously, is the big holdout. But extending that potentially, to a far broader block, which not only myself, but others have been postulating, would be a logical endpoint for where we were going under Trump grand macro strategy anyway.
turns.zh: 通过 USMCA（其中 Canada 是钉子户）、以及通过美洲（其中 Brazil 显然是那个大钉子户）去做的事，但把它潜在地扩展到一个大得多的集团——不只是我、还有其他人一直在推测，这本会是我们在 Trump 宏大宏观策略下走向的一个合乎逻辑的终点。

turns.en: But we try and cut to the chase. And if we get that, hey, we've cut to the chase. We were in two blocks fairly quickly. And if we don't, well, then things get really interesting and really messy. Michael, extending that analogy of the US acting as the global cop or the police force of the world,
turns.zh: 只不过我们试图直奔主题。如果真达成了，嘿，我们就直奔了主题，很快就形成了两大集团。如果没达成，那么事情就会变得非常有意思、非常混乱。Michael，把美国充当全球警察、世界警力的这个类比延伸一下，

turns.en: the cops go on strike, the criminals come out and start doing more crimes.
